places.name: Africa
places.significance: The text refers to 'africa bombings' as the event after which the US military/administration changed its view of UBL. The OCR is too garbled to say more.

events.description: Michael Scheuer sends a note to an excised recipient (likely Gary Schroen) lamenting the decision to forgo the capture operation against UBL after three chances in 36 hours.
Africa bombings, referred to in the text as the point after which the US military did not believe UBL was a problem. The OCR is badly degraded and the year is inferred.

The note says there were chances to get bin Laden three times in 36 hours, and each time the chance was forgone. It also says the administration passed up about half a dozen good-to-excellent chances to complete the operation.
The text refers to the Africa bombings. It says the US military did not believe bin Laden was a problem until they happened. The OCR is heavily garbled and the date is inferred, not stated.
A note was sent on 17 May 1999 to an excised recipient, likely Gary Schroen, expressing frustration at missed opportunities to capture or attack bin Laden.

relationships.detail: The CIA pursued bin Laden as a capture target and passed up several chances to carry out the operation.
relationships.quote: you and we will continue to pursue the target with determination

relationships.detail: The CIA is pursuing bin Laden as its target. The note says it will continue the effort and describes several missed chances to get him.

key_claims: The author says the capture operation against UBL was forgone despite three chances in 36 hours.
The author says the administration passed up about half a dozen good-to-excellent chances to complete the operation.
The author says the CIA director was effectively alone at the table, with the other principals deferring to his decision.
The author attributes the inaction to a stark fear of attacking a terrorist target and causing casualties.
The author says the forgone operation was the best opportunity yet to get bin Laden.
